out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed eating in the food prep area where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. The EHS discussed this with the PIC who will discuss it with the employee.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels a the bar area handsink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink in the first floor serving area being used to dump water in.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. The EHS discussed this with the PIC.

out_items.name: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated

violations.title: Package Integrity
violations.observation: The following food item(s) from damaged packaging were found offered for sale or service: observed a dented #10 can of food on the canned food storage rack in the dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Food packages such as canned goods shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants. Return all dented and damaged canned goods to your food supplier for a credit. The PIC removed the can during the inspection and returned it for credit to correct.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw unpasteurized shell eggs were stored over celery in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The PIC moved the raw eggs during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Hot Water Sanitizing Temperature Met
violations.observation: Due to improper operation of the hot water, mechanical warewashing machine, the thermolabel did not turn black, indicating that food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils are not being adequately sanitized. The hot water warewashing machine was tested three times and the final sanitizing rinse temperature never exceeded 153.9º.
violations.corrective_action: Immediately discontinue use of the dishmachine. Repair the dishmachine so that a thermolabel will turn black. Until the machine is adequately repaired, set up the 3 vat sink to manually wash, rinse and chemically sanitize food-contact surfaces. The PIC discontinued using the unit was will use the three compartment sink or the unit downstairs. Notify your EHS when the unit is repaired and working properly.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Two bottles of Fit veggie wash was stored with cleaning chemicals in the storage room. Fit is considered a food and should not be stored with chemicals.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The PIC moved the bottles of Fit during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: a squeeze bottle of cooking oil under the prep counter was not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. Label the squeeze bottle of oil as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Dead or Trapped Pest Removed
violations.observation: Several dead insects were observed trapped on a glue board on the second floor.
violations.corrective_action: Remove dead rodents, birds, and insects from the premises to ensure that the establishment is clean and sanitary and to prevent carcasses from attracting other pests. The EHS educated the PIC that glue boards must be changed frequently to remove dead and trapped insects. Discard the glue board with trapped insects as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Controlling Pests, Inspect Premises
violations.observation: The premises is not being routinely inspected for the presence of insects, rodents and pests. A live cockroach was observed in the second floor food serving and warewashing area. It crawled out from under the warewashing machine.
violations.corrective_action: Insects, rodents and pests are capable of transmitting disease to people by contaminating food and food-contact surfaces. Routinely inspect the premises to control the presence of insects, rodents and pests on the premises. The PIC stated his current pest control operator is not doing a good job and they’re looking for another one.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Packaged food was stored on the floor in the first floor bar area and in the dry stores storage room.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Discontinue storing foods on the floor. Move the items off the floor as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter. The solution for wiping cloths in the wait station area did not have any sanitizer in it.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: two pairs of tongs were stored on the oven door.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The PIC moved the tongs during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils Self-Draining Position/Covered/Inverted
violations.observation: Clean plates and silverware were observed stored uncovered in the second floor food serving area.
violations.corrective_action: Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored in a self-draining position that allows air drying and covered/inverted. The EHS educated the PIC on this requirement.

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils Air Drying
violations.observation: Plastic cups were found stacked while wet after cleaning and chemical sanitization.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food. The EHS educated the PIC on this requirement. BRIGHTVIEW WOODBURN (Inspection Date: 08/24/2026) Page 3 of 5

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items Storage and Handling
violations.observation: Tasting spoons in the food prep area were found handled, displayed or dispensed with the food or lip-contact surface facing upward. The spoons were being dispensed from the manufacturers case and the handles were not presented up or any other way to prevent contacting the lip contact surface while taking spoons out of the box.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items and cleaned/sanitized utensils shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of food and lip contact surfaces are prevented. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: there was a foul odor emanating from the grease trap piping or floor drain piping located in the storage room where single service items and chemicals area stored.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. Discontinue using the machine and use the three compartment sink or the dishwasher downstairs. Have the grease trap or floor drain piping serviced as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: the top shelf over the serving line was visibly soiled and in need of cleaning. The side of the two door prep unit was visibly soiled and in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean the shelf and the side of the refrigerator as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed that the following area were in need of cleaning: 1. The floor under the hood, 2. The wall under the hood.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Clean these areas as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Adequate ventilation and lighting, designated areas used

violations.title: Lockers, In Designated Room/Area
violations.observation: Observed that lockers and personal storage facilities are not located to protect food, equipment, linens, and/or single-service items from contamination. Employee belongings were being stored on food items being stored in the dry storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Relocate lockers and personal storage facilities to prevent the potential contamination of food, food equipment and utensils, linens, or single-service items. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

violations.title: Lighting Intensity, 50 Foot Candles Minimum
violations.observation: Observed that inadequate lighting was provided in the food preparation areas. There was one light bulb under the hood that was not working.
violations.corrective_action: Increase the lighting to provide a minimum of 50 foot candles in all food preparation areas. Replace the lightbulb to provide sufficient illumination under the hood. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: shrimp in the hot holding cabinet was 130°F
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The PIC reheated the shrimp in the oven to 165°F for hot holding. CDI.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: One of the servers was observed cutting fresh vegetables and preparing a salad without wearing a hair restraint.
violations.corrective_action: If food servers do not prepare foods, they are not required to wear a hair restraint. However, if they serve food and also prepare food, they must wear a hair restraint, just as other food preparers do. The EHS discussed this with the PIC.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system. There is a hose connected to a hose bib spigot in the kitchen next to the refrigerator. There was no vacuum breaker installed on the spigot. .
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. The EHS showed the PIC an image of the necessary vacuum breaker, which the PIC took a picture of. The hose was removed during the inspection to correct. Please install a vacuum breaker before reinstalling the hose. CDI.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Observed a food server handle clean pans from the dish machine, then load dirty dishes into it, then empty the clean dishes, then put on gloves and serve food for residents.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The employee should have washed hands after handling dirty dishes and before handling clean ones and again before serving food to residents. The inspector discussed this requirement and the importance of handwashing especially when working with a susceptible population such as at this location with the manager and the manager discussed it with staff.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided at the bar hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The manager provided paper towels at the bar hand sink during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no hand soap provided at the bar hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The manager provided hand soap at the bar hand sink during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: milk, cut melon, and one portion of salad with chicken were all above 41 degrees Fahrenheit in the Advantco one door refrigerator in the serving area. Milk was 47°F. Cut melon was 47°F. The salad was 48°F for two hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. Food in this unit was out of temperature during the last inspection. The manager discarded the milk and the cut melon. Since the chicken salad was made two hours ago, it was placed in the walk-in refrigerator.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the Avantco one door, upright display refrigerator in the serving area.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. Recommend having a technician check and assess this unit. Until it is capable of keeping foods 41°F or below, it should not be used to store TCS foods such as milk, cut melon, and chicken with salad.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: The clean pot storage shelf on the wall to the right of the hood system was visibly soiled with debris.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Please clean the shelf as soon as possible over before the next routine inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Half and half in 1 dr upright display cooler: 45 degrees F
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. NOTE: All TCS food in the cooler was relocated to the walk-in cooler.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: Avantco1 dr upright display cooler
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Observed staff entering the kitchen and not washing their hands before donning new, clean gloves.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS REMINDED STAFF AND MANAGEMENT TO MONITOR STAFF’S HAND WASHING PROCEDURES TO INCLUDE WHERE, WHEN, AND HOW. STAFF WASHED HANDS AFTER DISCUSSING.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that a sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at ONE KITCHEN handwashing sink used by food employees.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO PROVIDE A HAND WASHING SIGN BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, Clean before Use
violations.observation: The food employee failed to clean the food thermometer probe before use. Observed a staff member wipe the thermometer with a dry towel before checking leftover white rice for a reheating temperature.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned before using or storing a food thermometer. EHS INSTRUCTED THE STAFF MEMBER AND MANAGER THAT THE DIGITAL FOOD THERMOMETER(S) SHALL BE CALIBRATED AT LEAST ONCE A WEEK IN A CUP COMPLETELY FILLED WITH ICE AND SOME COLD WATER TO 32F. ONCE CALIBRATED THE THERMOMETER SHALL BE WASHED, RINSED, AND SANITIZED BEFORE TAKING FOOD TEMPERATURES. BETWEEN FOOD TEMPERATURES AN ALCOHOL WIPE IS ACCEPTABLE UNLESS TOUCHING RAW ANIMAL PROTEINS OR ALLERGENS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION AND STAFF ARE TRAINED BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION. BRIGHTVIEW WOODBURN (Inspection Date: 12/26/2024) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Proper hot holding temperatures

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) FOOD STORED IN THE HOT BOX TO BE TRANSFERRED UP TO RESIDENTS: A) MASHED POTATOES: 118F, B) PURÉED BEEF: 128F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO REHEAT FOODS TO 165F AND USE A CALIBRATED, CLEANED AND SANITIZED THERMOMETER TO VERIFY TEMPERATURES. EHS ALSO INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT THAT ANY HOT BOX USED TO HOLD FOOD SHALL BE SET AT 165F TO MAINTAIN HOT FOODS ABOVE 135F AT ALL TIMES.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Commercially Processed Food, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is commercially processed is not used or discarded within 24 hours of when the original container was opened and is not observed to be date marked: 1) OPENED PACKAGES OF COMMERCIALLY PROCESSED FOODS SUCH AS HOT DOGS, HASH BROWNS, AND OTHER PRE-COOKED POTATOES.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety commercially processed foods when opened and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of the original container was opened. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. This date cannot exceed any manufacturer determined 'use-by' date based on food safety. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT AND STAFF THAT ONCE ANY PACKAGES OF FOODS ARE OPENED AND RESEALED FOR REFRIGERATOR STORAGE, STAFF SHALL LABEL THEM WITH A DATE. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) DEEP PANS OF PREPARED FOODS LIKE CHICKEN SALAD AND TUNA SALAD ARE SEALED AND COVERED WHILE COOLING IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH THE MANAGER TO UNCOVER THE FOODS AND UTILIZE THE WALK-IN FREEZER TO FACILITATE RAPID COOLING OF FOODS. SEE FACT SHEET ON COOLING SENT VIA EMAIL. REMEMBER HOT FOODS SHALL COOL FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS OR LESS AND FROM 135F TO 41F IN NO MORE THAN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS. AMBIENT AIR FOODS LIKE TUNA SALAD THAT ARE ASSEMBLED SHALL COOL TO 41F IN 4 HOURS OR LESS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION AND TRAINING TO STAFF BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor inside the walk-in freezer.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO PROPERLY STORE BOXES OF FOOD ON SHELVES INSIDE THE WALK-IN FREEZER BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Wipings Clothes Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER TO STORE WET TOWELS IN THE RED BUCKETS WITH SANITIZER AT THE APPROPRIATE CONCENTRATION. ONLY CLEAN, DRY TOWELS MAY BE SITTING ON WORK SURFACES. ENSURE EACH WORK STATION HAS A RED BUCKET WITH SANITIZER FOR WET TOWEL STORAGE BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: 1) ICE CREAM SCOOP OBSERVED SITTING IN A STAGNANT CONTAINER OF WATER. THE WATER WAS NOT RUNNING AS REQUIRED.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS INSTRUCTED THE MANAGER THAT THE WATER NEEDS TO BE RUNNING CONSTANTLY. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE NEXT INSPECTION. BRIGHTVIEW WOODBURN (Inspection Date: 12/26/2024) Page 3 of 4

EHS HAD THE MANAGER TAKE A PICTURE OF THE APPROVED PRESSURE BLEED VALVE FOR THE MOP SINK. MANAGER WILL ORDER THE PART TODAY.
